findings.summary: The java.io.tmpdir pin does take effect for buildSrc's test task -- measured directly, not inferred: a temporary probe test read System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir") inside the forked buildSrc test JVM and it printed the buildSrc/build/tmp path, not /tmp (probe removed after measuring; repo restored and re-diffed to confirm the staged hash was unchanged by the measurement). No open finding on the pin's correctness -- your rule-17 fix is confirmed to take effect for buildSrc.
findings.failure_scenario: But no test in FreshCheckoutTest constrains this fact, so the fix rule 17 exists to make is not guarded going forward. Mutation performed: comment out the systemProperty("java.io.tmpdir", ...) line entirely (the exact regression this commit fixes, i.e. buildSrc reverting to unpinned). Result: all 13 FreshCheckoutTest cases still pass (verified with --rerun, tests=13 failures=0 errors=0). None of the 13 tests reads java.io.tmpdir or asserts a fixture path is under build/tmp rather than the system temp dir, so a future accidental deletion of this one line would go undetected by this suite and rule 17 would silently regress. Minor, not blocking: it is a coverage gap on a config line rather than a wrong assertion in a staged test, and review.md rule 12 / the M0.32 round-cap circularity already recorded argue against spending another round on a non-regression gap this round. Recommend a follow-up task asserting System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir") is under the project's build/tmp when running under buildSrc's own test task.
